description: A complete application with frontend, backend, and database. Examples: social bookmarking app, expense tracker, recipe manager, simple SaaS dashboard.

phases.core_concept: Full-stack architecture — frontend, backend, and database as separate responsibilities, and modeling the data for [PROJECT_PURPOSE] before building anything
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the initial project scaffold (folder structure, .gitignore, README outline)
Render an entity-relationship diagram from your finished table list
human_required_tasks: Draw the architecture: frontend → your backend → Supabase, and mark where every secret lives. NOTE: Secrets exist only in backend environment variables. If your diagram puts a key anywhere else, you are doing it wrong.
Model the data: the entities, fields, and relationships [PROJECT_PURPOSE] needs, with a user_id column on every user-owned table
Define the core user loop in one paragraph: what the user does, what your backend does, what changes in the database
explanation_gate_targets: Why your frontend touches the database only through your backend or the anon key with RLS, in your design
The entities in your data model and why each relationship exists for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
One user action traced through all three tiers of your app, from click to stored row
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured environment setup script (venv, dependencies, .env template) — skip the manual setup walkthrough at the start of Phase 2

phases.core_concept: How a FastAPI backend is structured — routes, request/response validation, startup config, and the service layer where all database calls live
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate FastAPI route boilerplate once the endpoint surface is decided
Generate Pydantic model stubs from your request/response field list
human_required_tasks: Decide the endpoint surface: which routes exist, their methods, and their request/response shapes for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
Write the config module that loads and validates every environment variable at startup
Wire the first endpoint end to end and test it in the auto-generated /docs
explanation_gate_targets: Why you chose these specific endpoints and shapes for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
What happens, step by step, when a request arrives at your API with an invalid payload
Why database calls live in a service module instead of inside route handlers in your project
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-configured FastAPI project skeleton with config validation and CORS wired — skip the configuration walkthrough in Phase 3

phases.core_concept: Turning your data model into a secure schema — Row Level Security and ownership policies before any query code is written
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the SQL for your schema after tables and ownership columns are decided
human_required_tasks: Enable RLS on this table and write an ownership policy before continuing. Do not proceed until this is done.
Create the tables from your Phase 1 data model, with a user_id ownership column on every user-owned table

Decide where the anon key and the service-role key are each used. NOTE: The service-role key bypasses RLS — it exists only in backend environment variables, never in frontend code or any committed file.
explanation_gate_targets: What your RLS policy actually enforces, and why 'user is logged in' is not sufficient — ownership must be verified
What happens if the ownership check were removed — what anyone holding your public anon key could read or write
Why the anon key is safe to ship in your frontend but the service-role key never is
How your schema enforces which user owns which rows
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Based on how you explained your schema, you've unlocked the advanced query builder — pre-written complex queries for your specific schema

phases.core_concept: Auth across the stack — Supabase Auth on the client for sessions, JWT verification on the server for security, and why only the server-side check counts
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate signup/login form markup and the client-side Supabase Auth calls
Generate the middleware boilerplate once the verification logic is decided
human_required_tasks: Write the auth verification middleware and attach it to every route that touches user data. NOTE: Hiding this in the UI does not protect it. This check must happen here, in the backend, on every request.
Wire the frontend session: store and refresh the session client-side and attach the token to every backend request
Run the two-account test: create Users A and B; with B's token, request A's resource ID. You must get 403 or 404, not data. Do not proceed until this passes.
explanation_gate_targets: What happens if the auth middleware is removed from one route in your backend — who can then do what
Why the frontend redirect to your login page is UX, not security, in your app
How the token issued at login is attached to a request and verified on your server, step by step
What your two-account test proved, exactly
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Your explanation of the authentication architecture was thorough enough to skip the basic session setup walkthrough in Phase 5 — here's the pre-configured session handler

phases.core_concept: Building UI that renders untrusted data safely — components, state, and escaping every piece of user-generated content
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the CSS layout and styling boilerplate
Generate repetitive component variants after the first one is written and understood
human_required_tasks: Write the rendering path for user-generated content. NOTE: Every piece of user content must be escaped or safely inserted (textContent, not innerHTML) — this is exactly where injection happens.
Design where state lives in your frontend and how views update when it changes
Design the loading, error, and empty states for [PROJECT_PURPOSE]
explanation_gate_targets: What specifically breaks if you render user content with innerHTML without escaping, in your UI
Where state lives in your frontend, and why you put it there
What the user sees when your backend errors, and how you built that path
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Pre-built list/table component styled for your project — skip the markup and empty-state handling for your main view

phases.core_concept: Connecting the tiers — a single fetch layer, consistent error handling, and keeping every secret out of the client bundle
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate the fetch wrapper once the API contract is decided
Generate loading-state boilerplate for your views
human_required_tasks: Define the API contract your frontend relies on and centralize all backend calls in one module
Confirm no secret appears anywhere in the client bundle. NOTE: .env values used by frontend build tools get bundled into JavaScript — anyone can extract them from the browser.
Decide how the UI handles auth failures globally: what happens on a 401 versus a 403
explanation_gate_targets: Why a .env file in frontend code does not protect a secret
What happens in your UI when a request returns 401 mid-session, and how you built that
Which environment values are safe in your frontend (Supabase URL, anon key) and which never are (service-role key, API keys), and why
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Advanced: pre-built optimistic-update helper for your list views — changes appear instantly and roll back on failure

phases.core_concept: Verification, not learning — confirming against your actual running app that every security constraint you built is really enforced before you ship
ai_appropriate_tasks: Generate a search script for secret patterns (api_key, secret, sk_live, token, password) across the codebase
human_required_tasks: Search the entire codebase for api_key, secret, sk_live, token, password. Confirm none appear in any frontend file or any file committed to the public repo.
Open browser DevTools Network tab. Make requests in the app. Confirm no secrets appear in any request or response payload.
Confirm all external API calls with secrets are made from backend functions, not frontend code.
Open Supabase Authentication → Policies. Confirm RLS is enabled on every table. Confirm every policy checks ownership, not just login status.
Attempt to access a protected route directly via URL or curl without being logged in. Confirm it returns 401, not data.
Attempt to access another user's data by manipulating a resource ID in a request. Confirm it returns 403 or 404, not the other user's data.
Confirm every user input that reaches the database uses parameterized queries, not string concatenation.
Confirm every user input that gets rendered in the UI is sanitized or escaped before rendering.
Run the app URL with /api, /admin, /dashboard, and other common paths appended. Document what responds and confirm nothing sensitive is exposed unintentionally.
explanation_gate_targets: Walk me through one item on this checklist. Tell me what you checked, what you found, and what you did or confirmed as a result.
Which checklist item surprised you or failed on first check in your app, and what you changed
Which single checklist item would be most damaging to skip for [PROJECT_PURPOSE], and what a stranger could do if you had skipped it
phases.unlock_condition: 3-turn gate passed with no unresolved follow-ups
phases.functional_unlock: Your gate scores across this project qualify you for the system design review — a full written architectural critique of your codebase you can reference in interviews
